nodes.description: Assess communication early and provide appropriate low- or high-technology aids, including access methods that adapt to progressive motor impairment. Speech-language and occupational teams should review needs and train the patient and carers. General ALS guidance is extrapolated to ALS27 with age-appropriate specialist judgment; it is not evidence of genotype-specific pediatric efficacy.

nodes.description: The mouse exon deletion models the human c.58G>T splice consequence. Heterozygotes lacked overt motor deficits through 15 months, had tested CMAP measurements at 17 months and no overt neuronal-loss/gliosis findings at 18 months. Four-month tissue lipid concentrations were unchanged in the measured classes. Among 100 offspring only three homozygotes were found; those survivors failed to thrive and died at 6–8 weeks. Prenatal loss was inferred from under-representation, not demonstrated by staged embryonic observation. No direct SPT activity or synthesis-flux assay established whether the allele increases or decreases enzymatic function in vivo.

nodes.description: Consider physical measures and, when appropriate, baclofen, tizanidine, gabapentin or other specialist-selected agents. Monitor sedation and increased weakness; focal botulinum toxin can be considered if other measures fail or are unsuitable. These are conditional general ALS recommendations, not evidence that every ALS27 patient has treatable spasticity.

nodes.description: Spasticity, hyperreflexia and pyramidal signs establish upper motor neuron involvement in many reported patients. These signs can be absent in individual cases, and upper motor neuron dysfunction need not precede weakness. Human clinical signs do not provide direct counts of cortical neuron loss.
